sectionHeadings: 021: Repair the truncated WAL append stream and the terminal-writer call paths
B-1. The entry stream has three endings, not two
B-2. A truncated append fails on both channels, exactly once each
B-3. A truncated append is terminal for the writer
B-4. A clean empty batch is a success and writes nothing
B-5. A terminal writer fails its callers rather than panicking them
B-6. What the persisted prefix is, and what it is not
B-8. A torn trailing record is recovered differently from a prefix, and tested
B-9. No acknowledgement in the WAL crate ends a thread, and a stalled test fails
B-7. A rejected append reports why, not that a channel closed
record.summary: Repairs F-028: the WAL writer could not tell a dropped entry sender from the marker that ends a healthy stream, so a truncated append was acknowledged and notified as a success. The writer now names the truncation on both channels and ends, and every adapter call path that panicked or waited on a terminal writer returns a named storage error instead. Amends 001 and 008 and carries their acceptance.
record.title: Repair the truncated WAL append stream and the terminal-writer call paths
